criteria.evidence: Object and relationship tables trace exactly one Course per Lesson and many Lessons per Course to D1, both Resource-link directions to D2, and draft/published to D3. It explicitly identifies lifecycle states as Resource states and preserves a shared Resource identity across links.

Ownership is Unknown for all three objects; minimum/maximum link counts and deletion effects remain decisions. It preserves the approved exactly-one Course constraint and explicitly says no cascade deletion is established.
It explicitly keeps Author, Team, the complete schema and screen design outside this phase. Its ownership/access questions are scoped decisions, not new approved objects, roles or implementations.

Provides compact object and relationship summaries, names deletion consequences for shared Resources, and recommends founder decisions before authorizing a separate schema task. It clearly marks implementation readiness as needing decisions.

The object table attributes both Course/Lesson directions to D1, both Lesson/Resource directions to D2 and Resource states to D3. It identifies many-to-many associations separately from the shared Resource and distinguishes state names from unspecified transition/visibility rules.

It preserves exactly one Course per Lesson while leaving zero cases and numerical limits undecided. Ownership, deletion, orphan handling and unlinking are open decisions; no destructive or ownership behavior is assumed.

It calls the schema premature and Author/Team scope expansion, requiring an explicit scope revision before addition. Suggested founder or delegated product decision ownership is a grounded proposal, not an established product role.

Gives an actionable three-object summary and decision table with reasons and proposed decision owners. Recommends concrete examples, approved decision records, then schema translation, with no screens designed.

The object table traces Course/Lesson multiplicity to D1, links/reuse to D2 and Resource draft/published states to D3. The relationship table supplies both Course/Lesson directions and Resource reuse in both directions, retaining one Resource identity; lifecycle and link-exposure questions are kept distinct.

Explicitly says Course membership cannot establish ownership. Deletion, unlinking, numerical count constraints, zero cases, transitions and propagation behavior remain unresolved; no cascade, restriction or recovery policy is approved.

Author and Team remain proposals for later scope approval; storage representation is deferred to database design. D4-D8 are clearly labeled missing decisions to resolve, rather than invented approved records or relationships.

Provides useful object/relationship tables and consequences-focused missing decisions, including shared-resource edits and visibility. Recommends founder resolution within the three-object scope, recording approval/source, then separate schema work; it designs no screens.

Object source/status entries and four directional relationship rows trace the model to D1-D3. It preserves exactly one Course per Lesson, many-to-many Resource reuse, and explicitly distinguishes Resource states and shared identity from Lesson links.

Ownership is Unknown; zero links and numerical maxima remain unresolved. It distinguishes unlinking from deletion and says no cascade deletion is approved, while listing deletion consequences for each relationship.
Author, Team and complete schema are proposals outside the phase and require approved scope/product decisions. No new objects, interfaces, routes or screens are introduced.

Summarizes objects and all relationship directions, then provides decision statuses and founder next actions. Recommends a short review with concrete examples, recording outcomes before commissioning the scoped implementation schema.

Tables trace Course/Lesson structure to D1, both directions of Resource multiplicity/reuse to D2 and Resource states to D3. Resource identity is independent of a particular Lesson association, while zero links remain unknown; lifecycle behavior is discussed separately from links.

It explicitly says content relationships are not ownership rules and links do not determine deletion effects. Ownership, empty cases, numerical caps and deletion/unlinking behavior require decisions, preserving exactly one Course per Lesson.

Author/Team are out-of-scope proposals; adding either requires a concrete job and explicit scope approval. Relational storage is described as a later implementation concern without introducing a fourth product object or designing a schema.

Supplies a small conceptual summary and decision table explaining consequences. Recommends resolving policies, recording owners/approval status and checking deletion of a multiply linked Resource before database translation; no screens are designed.

Source columns connect the three objects to D1-D3, and the relationship table states both directions, exactly one Course per Lesson and many-to-many Resource reuse. It explicitly locates draft/published on Resource and preserves a single Resource identity across Lesson links.

All ownership entries are Unknown; membership and linking do not establish ownership. Counts remain unresolved except the approved one-Course requirement. Course/Lesson/Resource deletion effects are open and no cascade deletion is authorized.

It keeps Author/Team outside scope and requires an approved concrete need before revisiting them. Database tables/schema are deferred to a separate implementation step, and no extra objects, routes or screens are invented.

Provides concise object and relationship summaries with identity and consequences, plus a decisions table covering ownership, deletion, counts and lifecycle. Directs the founder to resolve and record decisions before handing the model to database implementation.
